newsitem.title: USA: CBOT WHEAT CLOSES LOWER ON CORN AND SOY DECLINES.
newsitem.headline: CBOT WHEAT CLOSES LOWER ON CORN AND SOY DECLINES.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on a drop in corn and soybean futures, traders said.

Corn and especially soy were pressured by showers over the weekend in portions of the U.S. Midwest and on forecasts for more rain early this week in the key dry areas of the corn and soybean growing region.
There was some talk early Monday about showers in portions of Australia's wheat growing areas which could provide some relief to the crop there.

Wheat found underpinning from USDA's weekly export inspections report which pegged U.S. wheat inspected for export during the week ended Aug 7 at 30.037 million bushels, above expectations for 18 million to 22 million bushels.
But the overall export picture remains bearish for wheat futures.
"I think the market is disappointed in exports. We're 42 million bushels behind a year ago," said Charlie Sernatinger, analyst for E.D. and F. Man Interntional.
Wheat closed 1-1/4 to five cents lower, with September down 3-1/2 at $3.63-3/4 per bushel.

Cargill Inc sold one million bushels of September, FIMAT Futures bought two million December, sold two million December and sold two million September, traders said. E.D. and F. Man International bought 1.2 million bushels of December and sold one million December, sources said.

In spread dealings, Term Commodities did two million bushels of September/December at 15-1/4 cents, premium December and E.D. and F. Man International did one million September/December at 15-1/4 cents, premium December, traders said. Man also spread two million September/March at 25 cents, premium March, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 19,000 contracts, below the 21,626 traded Friday.

In wheat options, E.D. and F. Man Interntional bought 300 December $3.90 calls at 16 to 16-1/2 cents, Term Commodities sold 150 December $3.80 calls at 19-1/2 to 20 cents and Refco Inc sold 100 September $3.60 puts at 5-1/2 to six cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,450 contracts, below the 7,258 traded Friday.
